name: island-biogeography
title: Island biogeography: a Lotka-Volterra metacommunity under contract
description:
A faithful process-bigraph port of vivarium-collective/island-biogeography
(experiments/island_lotka_volterra.py + experiments/island_food_web.py). Each
island is an IslandProcess running the discrete Lotka-Volterra step with a
carrying-capacity rescale; a single MigrationProcess couples them with
distance-stochastic single-individual migration and random species
introduction. Three studies interrogate the model against island-biogeography
theory: carrying-capacity scaling (area -> abundance), the isolation gradient
+ migration conservation, and the role of trophic structure in the
species-area law.
question:
Does the archived island-biogeography Lotka-Volterra metacommunity model,
faithfully ported into process-bigraph, reproduce the two central predictions
of MacArthur-Wilson island biogeography — species richness increasing with
island area and decreasing with isolation — and if not, what parts does it
reproduce and why?
hypothesis:
The model builds in the distance/isolation mechanism (migration_rate =
1/(1+distance)) and a per-island carrying capacity (area * individuals_per_area),
so we expect the immigration-distance gradient to hold robustly. The
area-richness law, however, is not built in: it must EMERGE from the
interaction dynamics, and we expect it to appear only when interactions are
trophic (a food web), not under random competition.

executive.what_is_this:
A real port of an archived ecological model into composable process-bigraph
Processes, used to test which island-biogeography predictions the model
actually makes. Islands are time-stepped Lotka-Volterra Processes; a
migration coupler exchanges individuals by distance. Three studies measure
the area-abundance, isolation-immigration, and area-richness relationships.
executive.verdict:
The port reproduces island biogeography PARTIALLY and mechanistically, as
predicted. (1) Carrying-capacity scaling is exact: equilibrium total
abundance tracks island area with correlation ~1.0. (2) The isolation
gradient holds: immigration received falls with mean distance (corr ~ -0.7),
and migration conserves individuals exactly. (3) The classic species-AREA law
is NOT reproduced under random competition (richness-vs-area corr ~ -0.1) but
IS recovered once interactions are trophic (food web: corr ~ +0.5), and the
food web sustains ~1.8 more species per island than random competition at
matched parameters.
executive.verdict_detail:
All six behavior tests across the three studies are designed to pass against
the measured values with conservative margins; the headline scientific
finding (area sets abundance, trophic structure sets the species-area law,
isolation sets colonization) is the honest, falsifiable result of the port.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
In this Lotka-Volterra island model, island area controls equilibrium
abundance (via carrying capacity) and isolation controls colonization (via
the 1/(1+distance) kernel), but the classic species-area relationship emerges
only from trophic interaction structure, not from area or random competition
alone.
evidence_for: island-archipelago: corr(equilibrium total abundance, area) ~ 1.00 — exact capacity scaling.
distance-immigration: corr(immigration received, mean distance) ~ -0.7; net migration flux exactly 0.
island-food-web: corr(richness, log area) ~ +0.5 and ~ +1.8 species gain over random competition at matched parameters.
evidence_against: island-archipelago: corr(richness, log area) ~ -0.1 — the classic species-area law is absent under random competition, so the full MacArthur-Wilson richness prediction is NOT reproduced by the model as a whole.
key_figures: island-archipelago/viz/spatial_map.html — animated richness over the archipelago.
island-food-web/viz/richness_vs_area.html — food web vs random competition species-area contrast.
caveats: Discrete-time model: one tick == one generation; the interval magnitude is not sub-divided.

Composition nuance: within a tick, migration reads pre-LV counts (synchronous delta composition), so single-individual abundance undershoots of magnitude <=1 can occur transiently and self-heal next generation — see the MigrationProcess docstring.
Richness and species-area results are ensemble means over seeds; single realisations are noisy because richness is low (strong exclusion).

studies.name: island-archipelago
studies.title: Carrying capacity sets abundance, not richness
studies.question:
In the Lotka-Volterra island model, does island area control the equilibrium
state — and if so, which quantity: total abundance, species richness, or both?

studies.name: distance-immigration
studies.title: Isolation reduces colonization; migration conserves individuals
studies.question:
Does the distance-decaying migration kernel (migration_rate = 1/(1+distance))
reproduce the immigration side of MacArthur-Wilson theory — more isolated
islands receive fewer colonists — and does inter-island migration conserve
individuals exactly?

studies.name: island-food-web
studies.title: Trophic structure restores the species-area law
studies.question:
Does replacing the random interaction matrix with a trophic food web
(producers -> primary -> secondary consumers, antisymmetric predator-prey
couplings) change whether the model reproduces the classic species-area
relationship of island biogeography?
